subject: QBR prep: SLA runway, incident recap, and owner cadence
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR prep: SLA runway, incident recap, and owner cadence

Team,

We need a tight exec-ready bundle for next week's QBR covering the Nov 5 partial outage that affected several customers (notably Acme Analytics). My ask: a one-slide executive summary (what happened, customer impact, root cause, next steps and owners), a short SLA impact table (credits / exposures), and a list of action items with clear owners and deadlines we can present to the board.

Key facts (draft):
- Incident window: 2026-11-05 03:15 UTC – 2026-11-05 09:37 UTC (partial degraded responses, elevated p99 latency and some request failures).
- Immediate mitigation: scaled dedicated pool + rollback to previous autoscaler config; full traffic normalization by 09:37 UTC.
- Customers impacted: ~12 accounts with >1% request error spike; Acme Analytics reported query timeouts for scheduled jobs.
- SLA exposure: preliminary estimate ~0.7% of monthly availability lost for the affected shard; need final verification.

Attachments: draft postmortem digest and preliminary SLA heatmap attached. Please review and add concrete owner + target date for each action by EOD Monday so I can fold into the QBR deck. Vivek, can you provide a 2–3 line executive summary we can put on slide 1? Marissa, can you confirm the SLA math and add recommended customer outreach language. Rishi, please own customer communications for Acme. Hannah, please slot the slide into the QBR deck and coordinate a 30-min rehearsal.

Thanks,

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-digest.pdf (summary), sla-heatmap-nov.xlsx (prelim)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: SLA runway, incident recap, and owner cadence

Lauren —

Thanks, this is a good start. Suggested 2–3 line exec summary for the QBR slide: "On Nov 5 we experienced a partial degradation in request latency and error rate due to an autoscaling decision that failed to account for concurrent KV-cache warming. Mitigations (fast rollback, manual pool scale) restored service within ~6 hours; we missed one shard SLO. Planned mitigations include autoscaler safety thresholds, proactive cache-warming tests, and automated canary fallback logic."

Numbers to call out (prelim):
- p99 latency increased from 220ms -> 1.9s during peak; error rate peaked at 4.3% for affected customers.
- Estimated SLA credit exposure: currently estimating a one-off credit bucket (0.5–1.0% weighted across impacted accounts); Marissa, please confirm exact $ impact for Acme.

Suggested customer-facing language: short apology, root cause in plain English, steps taken, timeline for reliability improvements, and offer for account review/credit. Keep it concise — execs want the action and confidence.

I will own the root-cause bullet and the high-level actions. Marissa please own the SLA math and any dollar estimates; Rishi owns outreach. Hannah: I echo the rehearsal ask.

— Vivek
Head of Runtimes
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR prep: SLA runway, incident recap, and owner cadence

Adding SLA math and action-item roster. See inline: 

Action items (owner — target):
- Finalize postmortem narrative slide (Vivek — 2026-11-10 EOD)
- Confirm SLA exposure and $ estimate for Acme (Marissa — 2026-11-10 noon) -> prelim estimate: ~$4.2k in credits if we follow current credit policy; will refine by end of day.
- Customer outreach draft for Acme + approval path (Rishi — 2026-11-10 17:00) -> recommend 2 options: apology + service credit OR apology + one-week premium support.
- Autoscaler hard limit + safety thresholds (Eng infra) (Owner TBD; suggest Eng infra SRE squad) — plan due 2026-12-01.
- Canary fallback automation (ML infra) (Owner TBD) — MLP by 2026-12-15.
- QBR slide + rehearsal (Hannah — 2026-11-11 11:00 rehearsal)

Attachments referenced: postmortem-digest.pdf (two-page summary), sla-heatmap-nov.xlsx (per-customer exposure). I attached both to this thread and uploaded a copy to the shared QBR drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3CqQBR-QBR-Deck-2026

Notes on SLA math: preliminary approach uses weighted availability by shard and impacted request fraction; I flagged Acme as high-impact because scheduled queries missed their SLAs repeatedly during the window. If we go with the credit option for Acme, legal will need a short approval; Rishi, can you loop them in?

— Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-digest.pdf, sla-heatmap-nov.xlsx

Subject: Re: QBR prep: SLA runway, incident recap, and owner cadence

Thanks — I will own customer comms for Acme. Plan:
1) Draft outreach (apology + option A: service credit of ~$4.2k; option B: one-week premium support). Draft will be ready 2026-11-10 17:00 PT.
2) Open approval ticket SUP-2049 for the credit (copying legal).
3) Create a Jira parent ticket REL-9876 to track infra work: autoscaler safety + canary fallback; will create child tickets this week.

I will also join the rehearsal and will bring the recommended outreach wording. If Acme requests immediate credits, I will push the approval path but we should be prepared to offer the support week as a low-friction option.

— Rishi Malhotra
